title: YANG & RESTCONF on IOS XE
levelTitle: Level 28 - Cisco IOS and IOS XE

cards.q: What are YANG, NETCONF, and RESTCONF?
cards.a: YANG is a data-modeling language that describes device configuration and state as a structured tree, while NETCONF and RESTCONF are the model-driven protocols that read and write that model over the network, enabling programmatic configuration and telemetry.

cards.q: What is the difference between NETCONF and RESTCONF?
cards.a: NETCONF runs over SSH (port 830) using XML and RPC-style operations, while RESTCONF runs over HTTPS (port 443) using JSON or XML with RESTful methods such as GET, PUT, POST, and DELETE.

cards.q: What does a YANG data model define?
cards.a: A YANG model defines the device's configuration and operational state as a structured tree of nodes, forming the contract that NETCONF and RESTCONF operate on.

cards.q: Which commands enable NETCONF and RESTCONF on IOS XE?
cards.a: The commands are netconf-yang to enable NETCONF (SSH 830) and restconf to enable RESTCONF (HTTPS 443), with ip http secure-server for HTTPS support.

cards.q: What is the Cisco-IOS-XE-native YANG model?
cards.a: It is the Cisco native YANG model that maps directly to the device's native CLI configuration, compared to OpenConfig which is vendor-neutral.

cards.q: Which RESTful methods or NETCONF operations perform create, read, update, and delete?
cards.a: In RESTCONF, GET reads, PUT/POST/PATCH create or update, and DELETE removes; in NETCONF, get/get-config read and edit-config performs create, update, and delete.

cards.q: Why do YANG models and these protocols matter for network automation?
cards.a: They replace CLI screen-scraping with structured, model-driven configuration and streaming telemetry, enabling scripting, SDN controllers, and cross-vendor automation.

cards.q: Which commands verify NETCONF and RESTCONF state?
cards.a: show restconf, show netconf-yang sessions, and show netconf-yang datastore.

cards.q: A RESTCONF client cannot reach the IOS XE device; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: RESTCONF may not be enabled with the restconf command, HTTPS may not be available on port 443, or AAA/privilege is rejecting the client; check the config and reachability.

cards.q: What is the key exam distinction between YANG and NETCONF/RESTCONF?
cards.a: YANG is the data model describing the device, while NETCONF (SSH 830, XML, RPC) and RESTCONF (HTTPS 443, JSON, REST) are the protocols that transport it; they are different layers.

cards.q: What is the YANG/RESTCONF quick-review summary?
cards.a: YANG is the structured data model of the device, NETCONF transports it over SSH 830 with XML/RPC, RESTCONF over HTTPS 443 with JSON/REST, enabled with netconf-yang and restconf, and the native Cisco model mirrors the CLI.
